`Account`, `ServiceAccount` and `SelfHostedSync` are built from smaller pieces, all exported. Use them when
you need control the high-level classes don't give, for example your own storage of sync state, or the
sync loop over files that aren't vaults.

### Sync loop {#sync-loop}

```ts {linenos=false}
import { deserializeSyncState, passwordCredentials, serializeSyncState, syncKdbx } from "@openvireo/sdk";

const result = await syncKdbx({
  blob: client.database("personal"),          // or client.vault(id)
  db,                                          // your working copy; merged in place
  credentials: passwordCredentials(password),  // or several, newest first
  state: saved ? deserializeSyncState(saved) : null,
  onProgress: (step) => console.log(step),     // checking, downloading, merging, uploading
});
await persist(serializeSyncState(result.state));
```

`syncKdbx` is the desktop app's sync loop: a `HEAD` when nothing changed locally (`localChanged: false`), a
download, the rollback checks (revision and the sync generation inside the file), the three-way merge against
the base copy, the `If-Match` upload, and on `412` download, merge and retry (`maxAttempts`, default 5).
Persist `result.state` next to the file; it holds the ETag, the revision and the base copy for the next
three-way merge. The web app keeps it in IndexedDB with its cached database.

### Merge {#merge}

`mergeDatabases(local, remote, base)` is the merge on its own; see [Merge behaviour](/docs/sdk/merge-behaviour/). Like
the desktop app, the default mode doesn't apply permanent deletions (`mode: "synchronize"` does); deleting to
the Recycle Bin is a move and syncs normally.

### HTTP clients {#http-clients}

- `AuthClient` (`account.auth`) has a method for every account server route, and `TokenManager` refreshes
  access tokens and rotates refresh tokens.
- `SyncClient` (`account.sync`, `server.client`) covers every sync server route: `vault(id)` and
  `database(id)` return blob handles with `get`, `head`, `put`, `delete`, `history` and `getRevision`, and
  `subscribeEvents` opens the events stream.

Every client takes `fetch` (any `fetch`-compatible function, default `globalThis.fetch`) and `headers` to add
to every request, such as a `User-Agent` in Node.

### KDBX helpers {#kdbx-helpers}

The web app's helpers work on kdbxweb databases: `decryptKdbx`, `createNewKdbx`, `collectAllDbData`,
`addEntryToDb`, `editEntryInDb` (pushes the previous version to the entry's history first),
`deleteEntryFromDb`, group helpers, and `exportSelectedGroupsToKdbx`. For references and items:
`parseReference`, `readField`, `writeField`, `findEntry`, `parseItemReference`, `itemOf`, `listItems` and
`setItemFields`.

### Argon2 {#argon2}

Argon2id defaults to hash-wasm. At m = 64 MiB, t = 3 it took about 104 ms, against about 608 ms for
`@noble/hashes` (Node 24 and Bun 1.3, M-series Mac). `setArgon2Impl(nobleArgon2)` switches to pure JS
where WASM isn't allowed, and kdbxweb uses the same implementation (`initKdbx()`).

### OPAQUE module {#opaque-module}

OPAQUE runs in a small WASM module (about 118 KB, no imports) built from `packages/sdk/opaque-wasm/` with
opaque-ke 4.0.1. It uses the same suite as the account server and the desktop app (ristretto255, SHA-512,
Argon2id at libsodium's interactive setting), so records and logins work across all three. It loads lazily,
the first time a password is used. Bundlers need nothing special: `vendor/opaque/opaque-wasm.js` is a plain ES
module. Rebuilding it is described in `packages/sdk/vendor/opaque/SOURCE.md`.
